concepts.title: Nature of Thinking and Mental Imagery
concepts.definition: Thinking is the mental manipulation of representations -- concepts, images and symbols -- when the actual object is absent. It needs no immediate stimulus, works through internal symbols, and often borrows mental imagery, as when you picture your route home before setting out.
concepts.key_idea: Thinking moves the world inside the head -- absent objects handled as concepts and images.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy107.txt nature sections (describe the nature of thinking, mental imagery, concepts as building blocks, tools of thinking)
question_patterns: define thinking and list its characteristics
in class 11 thinking chapter: what are concepts and why are they called building blocks of thought
what is mental imagery give an example
how does thinking differ from perception
explain the role of language in thinking
describe a situation where you used mental imagery to solve a problem

solution_steps.explain: Thinking works on representations -- internal stand-ins for things not present.
Concepts categorise the world; images picture it; language symbolises and shares it.
Combining, comparing and transforming these tools is the work called thinking.

concepts.title: Reasoning and Problem Solving
concepts.definition: Reasoning draws conclusions from given information -- inductively from cases or deductively from premises. Problem solving runs through steps: identify the problem, represent it, form strategies like means-end analysis or algorithms, apply them and evaluate; mental set and functional fixedness are the classic obstacles.
concepts.key_idea: From premises to conclusions, from obstacle to strategy -- problem solving is thinking with a destination.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy107.txt reasoning sections (nature of thinking and reasoning, inductive deductive reasoning, steps of problem solving, strategies obstacles mental set functional fixedness)
question_patterns: distinguish inductive from deductive reasoning with examples
in class 11 thinking chapter: list the steps of problem solving
what is means end analysis as a problem solving strategy
explain mental set with an example
what is functional fixedness and how does it block solutions
solve a given problem by stating your representation and strategy

solution_steps.explain: Induction generalises from instances; deduction derives what must follow from premises.
Identify, represent, plan, execute and evaluate -- the standard route through any problem.
Watch for mental set -- old habits of solution -- and functional fixedness -- seeing objects in only one role.

concepts.title: Decision Making, Judgment and Creative Thinking
concepts.definition: Judgment and decision making weigh options under uncertainty, often using shortcuts that can bias us. Creative thinking breaks set: it is novel, useful and fluent, nourished by brainstorming, divergent production and tolerance of unusual ideas -- the opposite of rigid, convergent habit.
concepts.key_idea: Decisions use shortcuts; creation breaks them -- fluency, flexibility and originality mark the creative mind.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy107.txt decision sections (judgment decision making, shortcuts and biases, nature of creative thinking, brainstorming, divergent thinking)
question_patterns: how do people make judgments under uncertainty
in class 11 thinking chapter: describe brainstorming as a technique of creative thinking
give an example of a common shortcut or bias in decision making
suggest ways of developing creative thinking in students

solution_steps.explain: Judgments lean on availability and representativeness -- fast, useful, but systematically biased.
Creative thinking produces ideas both novel and appropriate; tests measure fluency, flexibility and originality.
Defer judgment, brainstorm quantities of ideas, seek unusual combinations -- divergent habits that feed creativity.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student insists on solving every maths problem with the first formula she learned, even when it does not fit. Name and explain the obstacle.

solution_template.explain: This is mental set -- a previously successful approach applied regardless of fit.
The habit blinds her to simpler or correct strategies the new problems need.
Representing each problem freshly -- asking what type it is before choosing tools -- dissolves the set.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A group must invent uses for a brick. Explain how brainstorming should be conducted to maximise creative output.

solution_template.explain: No criticism while ideas flow -- evaluation freezes divergent thinking.
Many ideas, including odd ones (doorstop, soil anchor, game piece), raise the odds of original ones.
Only after the flow stops do the group sift, combine and refine -- evaluation has its own turn.
